method: Audit all 130 names in the user-supplied missing-standalone column against the canonical graph. Names map only to explicit existing person IDs, with punctuation/accent folding and individually checked name variants. No fuzzy candidate was accepted automatically. Standalone status requires people[].node_id and a person-kind node. Roster/strand joins use the preserved person ID. This is a coverage audit, not a new historical source review or identity merge. Selected incidental references are examples, not an exhaustive full-text inventory.

claims.claim: Only 104 people have standalone person nodes
claims.qualification: 83 historians and 21 theorists; the other 1,251 indexed people have profile routes. A roster placement does not supply a standalone chronology or individual relationship graph.
Current revision has 79 schools and fields, 20 traditions and theories, and 203 entries overall; the feedback names revision 1.159.

Revision 1.135 added the Science Wars entry and objections/replies involving Kuhn, Latour, SSK, STS and historians of science. Existing source qualifications remain; this does not establish complete coverage of every counterargument.

Three group entries have reviewed_through 2024, while individual entries include selected later works and reception. Most group entries retain a 2000 review baseline. Later coverage remains selective; adding later dates does not establish a complete career review.

claims.claim: No Chinese or Japanese historiography among the people
claims.qualification: Huang and Wong have standalone entries engaging debates over Chinese history; Maruyama appears in intellectual history. These records do not establish systematic coverage of Chinese, Japanese, Korean or Islamic historiographical traditions. Do not infer nationality or tradition membership from a name.

claims.claim: Most named missing scholars are absent from the project
claims.qualification: All 130 lack standalone person nodes. Of them, 101 have existing roster profiles and 29 have no indexed person record. Several of the latter appear in sources or discussion only. Neither source mention nor profile presence supplies equal depth of historiographical coverage.

next_research_batches.purpose: Address traditions underrepresented in their own historiographical terms
next_research_batches.requirements: New source research into works, methods, exchanges and institutional contexts; include criticism and internal disagreements. These are research candidates, not accepted additions. Avoid placing distinct traditions in one umbrella or treating all non-Western scholarship as reaction to European theory.

next_research_batches.purpose: Deepen Black and Atlantic historiography across generations
next_research_batches.requirements: Build from existing roster IDs and sources, then establish individual chronologies and supported relationships. Preserve distinct historical projects and the existing reading limits.

next_research_batches.purpose: Give central methodological exchanges individual endpoints
next_research_batches.requirements: Promote existing profiles only after reviewing named works and disagreements. Preserve the distinct group entries and all existing IDs; do not mechanically redirect group-level arrows.

next_research_batches.purpose: Balance further expansion across the other named gaps
next_research_batches.requirements: Use the full candidate inventory to select bounded field-specific batches; canonical reputation or citation totals alone do not create a biography or influence relationship.
